Theme

Latin word

causā

causā (+ genitive)

ablative of causa, placed after a genitive: a noun, a gerund or a gerundive

for the purpose of, for the sake of

In this lexicon

  • purpose

    the recommended word · classical · Liv. 5.27.2: lūsūs exercendīque causā; Plin. Ep. 9.36.3: nōn tam vōcis causā quam stomachī

  • in causā esse: cause

    classical

  • causā + gen.: for

    classical

  • varietātis causā: for a change

    modern

  • meā causā: for all I care

    modern

  • animī causā: fun

    classical

  • Gaudeō tuā causā.: I’m glad for you

    classical

  • memoriae causā: remember

    classical

  • honōris causā: respect

    classical

Examples

  • is cum in pāce īnstituisset puerōs ante urbem lūsūs exercendīque causā prōdūcere

    he had made it his practice in peacetime to take the boys out in front of the city for play and exerciseLiv. 5.27.2
